[JAX] Use the new XLA autotuner cache flags for the persistent compilation cache.

XLA deprecated `xla_gpu_per_fusion_autotune_cache_dir` and `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_cache_mode` in favor of backend-neutral `xla_autotune_cache_dir` and `xla_autotune_cache_mode`.

Expose the new autotune cache `DebugOptions` fields in jaxlib and bump `jaxlib_extension_version` to 523. When jaxlib is new enough, JAX's persistent compilation cache now sets the new fields, and the cache key ignores them (both in `DebugOptions` and in `XLA_FLAGS`) the same way it already ignores the deprecated ones, so users switching to the new flags don't get cache misses. Older jaxlib versions keep using the deprecated fields.

The on-disk subdirectory name and the `jax_persistent_cache_enable_xla_caches` option values are unchanged, so existing caches and configurations keep working.

display_title: Migrate IFRT host-buffer cleanup callbacks to std::shared_ptr<const void>.

head_commit.message:
Migrate IFRT host-buffer cleanup callbacks to std::shared_ptr<const void>.

`xla::ifrt::Client::MakeArrayFromHostBuffer` and `MakeArraysFromHostBufferShards` previously documented that `on_done_with_host_buffer` and `HostBuffer::on_done` were invoked only when `OK` was returned, while implementations wrapped or executed them mid-call before validation and multi-shard creation completed. In addition, invoking `std::move(fn)()` on `std::function<void()>` left closure-captured host buffers alive until the enclosing `std::function` or `BasicStringArray` was destroyed.

Switch `MakeArrayFromHostBuffer` (renaming `on_done_with_host_buffer` to `host_buffer_hold`), `Client::HostBuffer::on_done`, and `BasicStringArray::OnDoneWithBuffer` to `std::shared_ptr<const void>` (with `MakeSharedCleanup` for callable-based cleanup) so ownership transfers unconditionally to the callee, cleanup runs deterministically on both success and failure once all readers finish accessing `data`, and callers already holding `std::shared_ptr` buffers pass them directly without extra wrapper allocations.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1021526713

This adds JAX regression tests for the upstream fixes when running with newer jaxlib versions.

head_commit.message:
Prepare JAX IFRT host-buffer callbacks for shared_ptr holds.

`MakeIfrtArrayFromShardsInBatch` previously invoked `HostBuffer::on_done` unconditionally before `pop_back()` when deduplicating identical host buffers across shards, throwing `std::bad_function_call` whenever `on_done` is null (such as with `force_copy=True` or Python scalars). Because all `HostBuffer::on_done` closures in `py_values.cc` release resources via RAII captures upon destruction, `pop_back()` already cleans up deduplicated entries safely.

In addition, prepare `py_values.cc` and `pjit.cc` for IFRT's upcoming `std::shared_ptr<const void>` host-buffer hold contract under `JAX_XLA_VERSION_NUMBER >= 89` by passing `py_buffer_ref` and `std::shared_ptr<std::vector<absl::Cord>>` directly instead of wrapping them in `std::function<void()>`.

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:TPU] Lower lax.ne on floats to arith.cmpf une

`_cmpf_lowering_types` mapped `lax.ne_p` on floating point operands to
`arith.CmpFPredicate.ONE`. `ONE` is ordered inequality, which evaluates to false
whenever either operand is NaN. JAX lowers `x != y`, `jnp.isnan(x)`, and
`jnp.nan_to_num(x)` through `lax.ne_p`, so SparseCore kernels returned false on
NaN inputs instead of true. That behavior disagrees with IEEE 754 and with
Pallas interpret mode.

Map `lax.ne_p` to `arith.CmpFPredicate.UNE` across all core types. Mosaic TPU
accepts `une` on TensorCore and lowers it to the same unordered compare
instruction already emitted for `one`, so TensorCore results do not change.
TensorCore lowering still falls back to `one` when `ctx.forward_compatible` is
set, when lowering without a backend, or when `libtpu` is older than `0.0.53`.
Comparisons without NaN operands do not change, and no flags change.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1021892456

`jnp.nan_to_num(x)` through `lax.ne_p`, so SparseCore kernels returned false on
NaN inputs instead of true. That behavior disagrees with IEEE 754 and with
Pallas interpret mode.

Map `lax.ne_p` to `arith.CmpFPredicate.UNE` across all core types. Mosaic TPU
accepts `une` on TensorCore and lowers it to the same unordered compare
instruction already emitted for `one`, so TensorCore results do not change.
TensorCore lowering still falls back to `one` when `ctx.forward_compatible` is
set, when lowering without a backend, or when `libtpu` is older than `0.0.53`.
Comparisons without NaN operands do not change, and no flags change.

display_title: Fix crash when deduplicating batched_device_put shards with force_copy=True.

head_commit.message:
Fix crash when deduplicating batched_device_put shards with force_copy=True.

When `MakeIfrtArrayFromShardsInBatch` deduplicates duplicate host buffer shards, it unconditionally invoked `std::move(host_buffers.back().second.on_done)()` before `pop_back()`. With `force_copy=True` (`allow_zero_copy=false`), `on_done` is an empty `std::function<void()>`, causing `std::bad_function_call`. When `on_done` is non-empty, its sole purpose is holding `py_buffer_ref` in its closure, which `host_buffers.pop_back()` already destroys.

display_title: [Pallas:TPU] Guard out of bounds and BoundedSlice VMEM refs in emit_pipeline

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:TPU] Guard out of bounds and BoundedSlice VMEM refs in emit_pipeline

In `pipeline.py`, `_window_aliases_source` previously returned `True` whenever the window memory space and the source memory space matched. For `VMEM` references, `BufferedRef.bind_existing_ref` aliased the source buffer through `BufferedRef.compute_slice`, which slices `ds(start, block_size)` without checking source bounds or `BoundedSlice` lengths. On non divisible `VMEM` dimensions or out of bounds `Element` steps, the tail step read and wrote past the `VMEM` allocation. On partial or empty `BoundedSlice` steps, `compute_slice` wrote the full static block size and overwrote untouched elements. In addition, `_create_bounded_slice` computed a negative remaining size when `slice_start` exceeded `dim_size`.

Update `_window_aliases_source` so `VMEM` windows with `BoundedSlice`, `Indirect`, unpadded tile aligned `Element`, or non divisible block dimensions stage through clamped `get_dma_slice` transfers while preserving `compute_slice` validation on padded `Element` specs and symbolic shapes. Default `VMEM` staging buffers in `_make_pipeline_allocations` to one slot when `pipeline_mode` is unset, and clamp out of bounds slices in `_create_bounded_slice`.

display_title: [jax] Fix checkify with shard_map under set_mesh and partial manual_axes

head_commit.message:
[jax] Fix checkify with shard_map under set_mesh and partial manual_axes

`shard_map_error_check` previously failed in two `jax.shard_map` configurations whenever a live error value flowed through the mapped computation:

- Under an active `jax.set_mesh` context, `expand_errors_leading_dim` was traced under `core.extend_axis_env_nd(mesh.shape.items())` without setting the manual abstract mesh, causing `lax.expand_dims` on manual-mesh error values to fail `check_avals_context_mesh`.
- When `shard_map` made only a subset of mesh axes manual (`axis_names` / `newly_manual_axes`), output error values were partitioned with `P(mesh.axis_names)` instead of only the manual axes, failing `shard_map` spec validation in eager mode and Shardy's `sdy.manual_computation` verifier under `jit`.

Trace `expand_errors_leading_dim` under the same manual axis environment and abstract mesh as `jaxpr_to_checkify_jaxpr`, and partition output error values with `P(core.order_wrt_mesh(mesh, manual_axes))`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/40907

name: CI - Wheel Tests (Continuous)
display_title: [jax] Fix csr_fromdense JVP for padded entries when nse > nnz

head_commit.message:
[jax] Fix csr_fromdense JVP for padded entries when nse > nnz

When `nse` exceeds the number of nonzeros, `_csr_fromdense_impl` masks the padded `data` entries to zero and records only the true nonzeros in `indptr` (`indptr[-1] == nnz`). `_csr_fromdense_jvp` did not apply the same mask: for padded positions `>= indptr[-1]`, `_csr_to_coo` produces `row = M.shape[0]`, which `_csr_extract` clamps to the last row `M.shape[0] - 1` of `Mdot` instead of returning zero. Because `CSC.fromdense` delegates to `csr_fromdense` on the transposed matrix, `CSC.fromdense` has the same bug. This produces nonzero forward-mode tangents and wrong forward-mode higher derivatives when `nse > nnz`.

Mask `data_dot` in `_csr_fromdense_jvp` with the same `true_nonzeros` mask used in `_csr_fromdense_impl`, matching the `_coo_fromdense_jvp` fix for https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/40624. Primal outputs are unchanged.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1021805101

display_title: Fix array base broadcasting in jnp.logspace

head_commit.message:
Broadcast a non-scalar base in jnp.logspace as NumPy does

jnp.logspace passed `base` straight to `power` with the linspace result,
so a non-scalar `base` was matched against the trailing dimensions of the
output instead of being broadcast with `start` and `stop` and expanded
along `axis`. Depending on the shapes this gave the wrong shape (a scalar
`start`/`stop` with a length-3 `base` gave (3,) instead of (3, 3)), paired
bases with the wrong start and stop values, or raised an error.

Do what NumPy does: bring `start`, `stop` and `base` to their common rank
and insert `axis` into `base` before taking the power. The scalar `base`
path is unchanged.
